Maria (Support): hey team — customer reports GitHub OAuth failing at callback with a 403 'state mismatch'. They say flow starts fine, then on redirect back to our /oauth/callback the `state` query param is different than what we set. repro steps from customer below.

Maria (Support): Repro steps they provided: 1) Click 'Sign in with GitHub' 2) GitHub redirects to https://app.example.com/oauth/callback?code=...&state=eyJw...<truncated> 3) Our logs show saved_state=eyJw...A== but incoming state=eyJw... (different length). Happens intermittently, mostly behind their corporate proxy. They can reproduce in Chrome but not in Firefox.

James (SRE): can you paste the exact redirect URL the customer got (sanitized)? Also which proxy/vendor? corporate proxy often rewrites or clamps URL length.

Maria (Support): pasted (sanitized): `https://app.example.com/oauth/callback?code=abc123&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJzdWIiOiIxMjM0NTY3ODkwIiwibmFtZSI6IkpvZSJ9.` — note trailing dot, then it ends. customer says some clients drop padding `=` at end.

Devon (Eng): looks like our state is a base64url-encoded JWT-ish payload plus PKCE thumbprint. We expect padding or URL-safe base64. If a proxy or browser strips `=` padding or truncates at `.` that could cause mismatch. Also some corp proxies treat `.` as separator when rewriting? weird.

James (SRE): can we confirm how we persist state? in Redis with key `oauth:state:<state>`? and expiration 5m? if so check our logs for create vs consume. Maria, can you attach our create/consume log lines around that timestamp?

Maria (Support): pasted logs (sanitized):
```
[2024-04-03T15:21:10Z] create_state key=oauth:state:eyJhbGciOi... value=uid:12345 pkce=E9MelHa... ttl=300
[2024-04-03T15:22:05Z] consume_state incoming=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpX.... result=NOT_FOUND
```

Devon (Eng): NOT_FOUND suggests state was mutated en route. Can the customer repro with curl (no proxy)? request URL will show exact bytes: `curl -v "https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=https://app.example.com/oauth/callback&state=..."` then copy redirect Location header.

Maria (Support): customer tried curl from their network and it failed too. they confirmed the Location header arriving at their edge has full state, but their edge strips trailing `=` when forwarding to our origin.

James (SRE): aha — sounds like their reverse proxy (they said F5 BIG-IP) is normalizing/cleaning querystrings. Some setups drop `=` as they think it's padding. Two options: 1) make our state shorter/URL-safe without padding (use base64url without `=`) and avoid characters proxies mangle, or 2) fallback to storing state server-side keyed by a short ID sent to the client (short token in query param).

Devon (Eng): quick mitigation: accept both padded and unpadded variants when validating state (try adding `=` padding back before lookup). Example fix: `function normalizeState(s){ return s.replace(/-/g,'+').replace(/_/g,'/').padEnd(Math.ceil(s.length/4)*4, '=') }` — but careful with security: only normalization, don't accept arbitrary changes.

Maria (Support): customer wants patch ETA. they said this blocks SSO for ~200 users.

James (SRE): we'll patch normalization in auth-consume handler and add metrics for state mismatch counts. I'll open a quick canary. Devon can you send a small PR?

Devon (Eng): PR opened: `fix/auth-state-normalize` — adds normalization and extra logging of raw incoming state (truncated to 256 chars) and original redirect URL for debugging. Also added a test for padded/unpadded comparisons.

DeployBot: deployment scheduled to canary hostgroup at 2024-04-04T02:00Z. commit: ab12cd3.

OAuth Audit Bot: audit event: oauth_state_mismatch_detected count=1 metadata={client:github, network_hint:customer-corp-proxy}.

James (SRE): follow-up plan: 1) release normalization to canary, monitor SLOs & mismatch metric 2) reach out to customer with workaround: switch to POST callback (if they can) or ask their infra to allow query `=` padding 3) medium-term: change state format to short random id referencing server-side store to avoid encoding issues.

Maria (Support): shared workaround to customer (instructions + ETA). Customer replied :thumbsup: and will test tomorrow. thanks all!

Devon (Eng): note for backlog: audit our OAuth docs recommending base64url (no padding) or using URLEncoding for state. Also add a note about proxy edgecases.

Maria (Support): closing thread when canary passes.
